# SORA Nexus secp256k1 compatibility adapter

This new package retires the unmaintained `libsecp256k1` implementation in favor
of maintained RustCrypto `k256` 0.14.0. The recommendation comes from
[RUSTSEC-2025-0161](https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2025-0161.html).
It contains only the byte-oriented compatibility API needed by this repository;
all curve arithmetic, secret-key ownership, deterministic signing, verification,
and recovery are performed by k256. It is not a renamed copy of the retired
implementation. The crypto-bigint dependency enforces the 0.7.6 security floor.

Historical protocol behavior is intentional:

- Messages are reduced modulo the curve order before RFC6979 signing.
- Standard signature parsing permits zero scalars, but verification and recovery
  reject them. Overflowing parsing reduces the two scalars, as required by v1
  runtime recovery host functions and deprecated historical verification.
- Verification accepts high-S signatures. Recovery retains both recovery bits,
  including rare IDs 2/3; changing S to n-S requires flipping the parity bit.
- Full SEC1 hybrid public keys retain their historical parity validation.
- Secret keys use k256 ownership and zeroization; Debug does not reveal them.

SDK sp-core, SDK sp-io, smoldot, common, the node, and the bridge/rewards pallets
use this package through existing local dependency aliases. The unused
bridge-types dependency was removed. The bridge test helper reads R/S from
serialized bytes instead of the retired implementation's public scalar fields.
No legacy curve implementation is present in an active dependency graph.

Validation on 2026-10-24: six checked-in regression tests pass, as does a
`--no-default-features --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` build. A separate
historical-reference program passed 14,094 deterministic compatibility checks,
including 1,024 byte-identical signatures and recovery IDs. It compares all
recovery IDs, high-S recovery and verification, canonical/overflowing scalar
parsing, malformed lengths, hybrid public keys, and digest/order boundaries.
The eight fixed signature fixtures and four rare-recovery fixtures were captured
from unmodified libsecp256k1 0.7.2, not generated by the replacement.

Reference archive SHA-256:

- libsecp256k1 0.7.2: `e79019718125edc905a079a70cfa5f3820bc76139fc91d6f9abc27ea2a887139`
- k256 0.14.0: `93f50113171a713f4a4231ef82eb26703607139b35dcb56241f0ceab2ae1f7d8`
- Differential transcript: `f6a5fb45b886c56224b89648ae0b8fd5aacb595e49d02909d2dc4d3ab8516962`

To reproduce the optional reference comparison, run from the repository root:

```sh
python3 vendor/sora-secp256k1-compat/verification/compare_legacy.py \
  --workspace /tmp/sora2-libsecp-differential \
  --target-dir /tmp/sora2-rustcrypto-migration-target
```

Only this explicitly invoked, external temporary workspace resolves the retired
reference library. The checked-in regression tests need only the maintained
adapter and k256, and can run with `cargo test -p sora-secp256k1-compat`.
